---
title: "Luna Wang"
---

I'm a PhD student at the University of Toronto's Institute for the History and Philosophy of Science and Technology (IHPST).

My work sits at the intersection of the philosophy of biology, philosophy of cognitive science, and philosophy of technology. I study agency, consciousness, and cognition, and the diverse forms in which they appear across living and artificial systems. Recently, I am exploring the role of language, semiotics, and communication in shaping sense-making, especially in intersubjective and sympoietic contexts. Through this work, I hope to develop a richer understanding of human–AI relations and the ways in which interactions with artificial systems affect human agency and sense-making.

## Areas of interest

- Enactivism and embodied cognition
- Biosemiotics
- Metascience, theory construction and quantitative modeling
- Process-relational philosophy
